title: Open sign-in admits everyone while a JoomlArt member is labelled for /ops and keeps their marketing source
steps: S1: With TEST_DATABASE_URL set, sign in by email code as an address aMember reports as a member (gate off and legacy BETA_GATE=on), twice.
S2: Sign in through the Google callback as a member and as a non-member.
S3: Ask for a code with utm fields, verify it after BETA_GATE flips.
expect: S1: every verify is 200, no beta_login_job row, one account.first_sign_in signal labelled 'JoomlArt member' with plan 10, exactly one aMember call across both sign-ins, the code never in the signal.
S2: both are admitted; the member is 'JoomlArt member', the non-member 'gate off'.
S3: 200, the signal keeps the marketing source and carries the member label.
evidence: develop red since #1466 (run 39252256196): four tests expected 'gate off' for a member after #1457 started labelling members with the gate open
fence: The open gate never refuses anyone and the membership lookup only labels: a member reads 'JoomlArt member', a non-member 'gate off', the source survives

tests: public email sign-in: no queued check, one cached lookup labels the member, one first-sign-in signal
Google callback admits non-members and records the provider once
legacy gate on: public sign-in preserves the marketing source without a queued membership check
a code keeps its marketing source when legacy BETA_GATE changes between request and verification
